name: short log section (fallen log / stump), natural map prop for the Beodeul 16px chipset, 2x1 tiles, standing object (3rd layer), 3/4 top-down, sits on grass between broadleaf trees
label: beodeul_organic/log-short

refSet.reason: 칩셋 beodeul_organic 의 화풍 기준 묶음이 없다

surfaces.part: log trunk upper surface (lit bark ridge)
cut end face (pale rings, left end)

answer.evidence: The main body is a horizontal log, rows 5-14, 26 px wide. Its upper rows 6-8 are lit bark that is lighter (L 98-131 at x=9, 16 and 22) and the shading steps down to a darker mid-tone at rows 8-9. That reads as the upper surface, with a darker front bark face below it (rows 9-14, ending in the darkest shadow rows 12-14). There is no crisp 1-row front-edge line, so the top is rounded and modest, about 3 rows. At the west end, the pale cut face is a rounded shape (about 5 columns wide, rows 6-13) with a ring highlight. It shows the end of the log as a receding side face, so the log is not a flat profile. The silhouette is 22-26 px wide with a rounded bottom (rows 13-14 narrowing from 20 to 10), which gives it volume. The branch stub on top (rows 3-5) is decor. It is borderline between a rounded-cylinder top and a front elevation, but the highlight band with a darker face below it, together with the visible end face, favours three_quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small log about 2x1 tiles, so the per-tile facts read 0 and I judged by eye. It has a cut end with ring detail and a bark body in about 4 brown steps, with a darker underside and a lighter top. The outline is a dark brown tint and not neutral black, which matches the dark-material-tone approach, but it is fairly uniform around the whole silhouette, so I call it mixed. Texture is limited to a few bark streaks and rings. Next to the references, which carry 6+ steps, clustered leaf and bark grain and many visible tones, the log is thinner and flatter. The bark body has few grain dots and no moss, grass overlap or per-section highlights, so it reads somewhat like a sticker. It is cleanly drawn, but a careful artist would likely want more bark grain and ramp steps before placing it beside the references. When in doubt, fail.

surfaces.part: log body front face (bark, shaded underside)
pale cut end ring at left, drawn as an oval

answer.evidence: The silhouette width grows from 2-3 px at rows 3-4 to 22-26 px at rows 6-10, then narrows to 10 px at row 14. This is a lying cylinder. The top is a lighter bark band at rows 5-7, with a lighter edge row at 6-7 (x=9 L=131 at row 7, x=16 L=131 at row 6). Below it are mid-dark rows 8-11 and the darkest rows 12-14, which form the front and underside, about 8 rows. The pale oval at the left end (rows 6-13) is the cut end, drawn as a visible end face. The top band is thin and the shading is cylindrical rather than a flat plane with a hard eave, so the top reading is modest but present.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small log under 2x1 tiles, so the per-tile tone count is 0 and I judged by eye. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans dark brown beside the wood. That fits the Beodeul approach and is not a sticker line. The 14 distinct colours are about the same as tree-1a786c (10), but tree-d43edd is far richer (29 visible tones per tile, 567 colours). The body reads as a roughly four-step brown ramp: a highlight along the top, a mid tone, a darker underside and a lighter cut end with a ring. Bark grain is only a few sparse lines, with no per-clump or per-patch highlights, no moss or knots, and no grass tufts or soil grain at the base. Next to the references' multi-tone trunks and roots, it looks slightly thinner and smoother, closer to a tidy cylinder than a worked-over natural prop. No large flat fills were measured (0% near-flat), but the shading is shallow for the Beodeul bar, and I fail it when in doubt.

surfaces.part: log trunk upper curve (bark top highlight)
cut end grain disc at left

answer.evidence: The log lies east-west. surfaces.part: cut end face (pale ellipse, west end)

answer.evidence: The silhouette widens from 11 px at row 5 to 26 px at rows 8-10, then narrows to 10 px at row 14.
